## Rule

**Translate the grid DOWN by one row** (zero-fill the vacated top row). NOT a roll, NOT a
3-cycle permutation, NOT a mirror — the older "row 3-cycle / roll" framing in the prompt and
the SPREAD scan is **wrong** and is what tempts the dead-end cost-4 Slice-reverse trick.

ARC-GEN source (`external/ARC-GEN/tasks/task_25ff71a9.py`): `output[r+1][c] = grid[r][c] = color`,
with live pixels placed only in input rows 0–1 (`common.all_pixels(size, size-1)`). Both grids are
**always 3×3** (`size=3`; verified 60/60 real pairs). Consequences:
- input row 2 is **always all-background** (no colored pixel can land there);
- output row 0 is **always all-background**; output = input with rows shifted down 1, the
  (always-background) input row 2 falling off the bottom.

**Encoding (decisive).** The official `neurogolf_utils.convert_to_numpy` one-hot encodes *every*
cell including color 0: `benchmark[0][color][r][c] = 1.0`. So **background cells carry `ch0=1`**;
only the out-of-grid padding (rows/cols ≥ 3 for a 3×3 grid) is all-zero. This is the entire reason
a geometric `Pad` shift fails (see Don't-do) and why the Gather must *source* the background top
row from a real background input row rather than synthesize zeros.

## Algorithm sketch

```
# Shipped solution — single Gather on the row axis (axis=2), index length 30.
idx = [2, 0, 1] + [29]*27          # len 30
output = Gather(input, idx, axis=2)
#  out row 0  = in row 2   -> active-background row (ch0=1 @ cols0-2) == output's bg top row
#  out row 1  = in row 0
#  out row 2  = in row 1
#  out rows 3..29 = in row 29 -> padding (all-zero)   [27 trailing 29s]
# memory 0 (Gather output IS the graph 'output', which scoring exempts) + params 30 = cost 30.
```
The index reuses input row 2 (a genuine background row in the ch0=1 encoding) as the new top row,
so no constant and no intermediate are needed. That reuse is what makes cost 30 the floor (below).

## Cost analysis

`cost = memory + params`. The Gather's output is the graph `output` (scoring exempts tensors named
`input`/`output`, so memory = 0); its only cost is the length-30 INT64 index initializer (params =
element count = 30, dtype-irrelevant). So **cost 30 = 21.5988 pts**, and the floor question is purely
"can the row-shift-with-background-fill be expressed with < 30 total params+memory?"

### Floor proof — cost 30 is optimal (no sub-30 exists)

Same standard/structure as the recolor-floor (`cost_floor_reference.md`) and `task337.md` proofs:
strong structural argument + exhaustive measurement of the candidate families.

**Case A — one node, `input`→`output` directly (the only memory-0 shape):** enumerate ops that map
`[1,10,30,30]`→`[1,10,30,30]`:
- `Gather` on the row axis: a 30-row output needs a 30-element index ⇒ **30 params** (dense). Sparse
  index (29) is **rejected** by the pipeline (measured). A channel/col-axis Gather can't move rows.
- `Slice`: output rows are a *strided arithmetic* sequence; the needed source order `[2,0,1,29,…]`
  is non-arithmetic, and Slice can't synthesize the ch0 background row ⇒ impossible.
- `Pad`: a translation, **but DIVERGES** (see Don't-do) — a scalar pad fill can't make the per-channel
  `ch0=1` background row, and the shift leaks active-bg input row 2 into output row 3 ⇒ impossible.
- `Transpose` (0 params): permutes axes only, can't move data within the row axis ⇒ impossible.
- depthwise `Conv` (group=10, `[10,1,2,1]`): a down-shift with only **20 params** (< 30) — DIVERGES
  2060/2060 (measured). A geometric conv zero-fills the vacated row (same ch0 failure as `Pad`); a
  per-channel bias is uniform over all positions so it can't inject ch0-bg in row 0 only. Non-grouped
  `Conv`/`Gemm` shift kernels are ≥300/≥900 params anyway.
- `Scatter*`/`Reshape`/`DepthToSpace`/`Resize`/pooling: need index+updates / shape inits / can't realize
  an intra-row shift with this fill ⇒ ≫30 or impossible.

**The real obstruction (key insight):** it is **not** the param-count of the shift operator —
sub-30-param shift ops exist (`Pad` 0–9, depthwise `Conv` 20). It is that **every geometric shift
zero-fills**, and under the ch0=1 background encoding the vacated band must read as *background*
(`ch0=1`), which zero-fill never produces (and the shift also drags the active-region's own bg row
into the padding band). The ONLY correct primitive is one that **relocates an existing background row**
into the vacated band — i.e. `Gather`/`Slice` of a real bg input row. A single `Gather` doing this for
a 30-row output needs a length-30 index ⇒ **30 params**. ⇒ cheapest *correct* single op = **30**.

**Case B — ≥2 nodes (≥1 counted intermediate `I`, so memory ≥ 1):** the reorder must be performed by
*some* node:
- by a `Gather(input,…)`→`output`: still needs the 30-element index. As an init ⇒ 30 params (+mem(I) ⇒
  >30). As a computed intermediate `idx[30]` ⇒ INT32/INT64 = **≥120 B** (>30).
- by `Slice`/`Concat`/`Pad` on data: any intermediate that helps assemble a 30-wide-row, 10-channel
  output is ≥ `[1,10,1,3]` BOOL = **30 B**, and realistically the F32 reconstruction box is
  `[1,10,3,3]` = 360 B (measured: gather3_pad 3603, slice_concat 7205).
- a sub-30-byte intermediate (scalar / `[1,10,1,1]` / `[1,1,3,3]`) **cannot** enable the shift: the
  final op would be either elementwise(input, tiny) — no shift possible — or Gather(input,…) — needs the
  30-index again.
  ⇒ Every ≥2-node graph costs **>30**.

**∴ min cost = 30**, realized uniquely (up to index dtype/representation) by the shipped single Gather.
Caveat: this is a structural+empirical proof (not a machine-checked enumeration of all ONNX graphs),
matching the rigor bar of the other floor proofs in this repo. **Do NOT re-hunt sub-30 for task053.**

## Don't-do log

_Record ruled-out hypotheses here so future agents don't retry them._

**2026-06-01 THE TRANSLATION → `Pad` TRAP (worker-7): cost-0 / cost-9 but WRONG on 100% of inputs.**
The true rule is a down-shift (a translation), and translations are *usually* a single cheap `Pad`
(opset-10 `Pad` carries `pads` as an **attribute** ⇒ 0 params; the node output is `output` ⇒ 0 memory ⇒
**cost 0, scores the 25.0000 ceiling**). It is a **catastrophic trap here**: measured **2060/2060
divergence** (and 60/60 on real pairs). Root cause = the `ch0=1` background encoding
(`convert_to_numpy` one-hots color 0): (a) output row 0 must be the active-background row `ch0=1` at
cols 0–2, but a scalar `Pad` fill is all-zero; (b) the shift drags input row 2 (an active-bg row,
`ch0=1`) into output row 3, which must be padding-zero. A geometric pad cannot create or relocate the
`ch0` background signal — only the Gather (which *fetches* input row 2 to the top) can. **Generalizes
to every translation/shift task in this competition: `Pad`-shift is only byte-correct when the encoding
treats background as all-zero; with the standard ch0-hot background it silently produces a max-scoring,
100%-wrong network.** See `Onnx_Advanced/traps.md` and the "shift/translation floor" note in
`cost_floor_reference.md`.

**2026-06-01 cost-4 Slice-reverse exception does NOT apply (worker-7).** The channel-reversal cost-4
`Slice(steps=-1)` trick (`cost_floor_reference.md`) only fits an exact reversal `[9,8,…,0]`. task053's
active-row map is `[2,0,1]` (a down-shift), not the reversal `[2,1,0]`; `slice_reverse` diverges
2051/2060. Sparse Gather index (NNZ=29) is rejected by the scorer (`score_network_v2`→None).

**2026-05-19 crop-to-active-grid (worker-7, Group S sweep): NOT VIABLE.**
All internal intermediates already operate at 3×3 or smaller (earliest Slice already crops).
The only [30,30] tensor is the model OUTPUT, which ORT does not bill in activation memory.
Prepending a Slice(input→[1,10,3,3]) adds a 360-byte intermediate without removing any,
increasing cost. Verified: task087 crop-test went 376→748. Do not retry crop on any Group S task.
_(Note: this entry predates the rule correction above; "crop" is moot anyway since the shipped graph
is already a single Gather with zero intermediates.)_
